text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) is among the first airlines in the world to install advanced safety equipment the so-called Enhanced Ground Proximity Warning System (EGPWS) a navigation system controlled by satellite. EGPWS is to be installed in all SAS aircraft within the next six to nine months.

--- Danish exporters and haulage firms are nervous of trading with Russia because of non-payment of invoices, difficulties woith custims authorities and the difficulty of insuring loads. Therefore the Danish Confederation of Industry (DI) and the ministry of transport are holding a conference, with Russians, to seek solutions. Exports to Russia increased by 17.3 percent in the first six months of 1996 to nearly four billion crowns, but could be much more if exporters felt more secure, DI says.

--- Danish cancer specialists have achieved impressive results in treating patients with skin and kidney cancer according to a new therapy in which the patient's own immune defence mechanism is used to fight the cancer.

--- The number of children attending private schools is larger than ever. 13 percent of all schoolgoing children now attend fee-paying schools and many private schools have no room for new pupils in years to come.
--- A new survey from Sonar among 122 large export companies shows that a majority believe Denmark will enter the European Monetary Union despite its current rejection.

--- French airline Air France is to increase competition against Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) by increasing traffic between Copenhagen and Paris with a campaign which is to attract new business passengers. Air France has 39 percent of passengers on the Copenhagen-Paris route compared to SAS which has 55 percent.
